thread:
alex: Quick Q — I'm hunting for raw logs for a single request_id (x-rw-req: abcd-1234-ef). Is there a go-to flow in Console or is redwoodctl still faster? I also have trace id trace-0xyz if that helps.
maria: Console is easiest for quick eyeballing — Observability → Traces, paste the trace id, open the trace view and use the "Related logs" / "Open in Logs" button on the right. Make sure to set the timeframe (top-right). https://console.redwood.ai/observability/traces :sparkles:
kai: CLI flow is solid for scripting. Example:
```
export REQ=abcd-1234-ef
export RW_PROFILE=prod
redwoodctl logs query --req-id $REQ --env prod --since 15m --json | jq .entries[]
redwoodctl traces fetch trace-0xyz --json
```
Tip: add `--limit 500` if you expect lots of lines.
engbot: deploy-bot: heads-up — `redwoodctl` requires an SSO session or machine token. Run `redwoodctl login` (or set RW_TOKEN) before querying.
maria: If you only have the request_id (no trace), use Logs → Search in Console and filter `req_id:abcd-1234-ef` + `service:api`. Click any log line that has a span/trace link to jump to the trace. Use timeframe presets (last 1h) to narrow down.
devin: Also remember the internal mapping endpoint if you have access: `/internal/req2trace?req_id=abcd-1234-ef` — returns trace id(s). If you don't have access, ping @platform oncall. In traces JSON you can also look for span tags like `req_id` or `x-rw-req` to correlate.
alex: Worked — redwoodctl found the logs (used `--since 30m` + `--pattern ERROR`). Found the failing span. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
kai: One-liner for terminals if you want a compact table:
```
redwoodctl logs query --req-id $REQ --env prod --since 30m --json | jq -r '.entries[] | [ .ts, .service, .msg ] | @tsv'
```
maria: if you hit slow console load, try increasing the timeframe granularity or use `service:api AND level:ERROR` filters first. Saves clicks.
alex: saving these steps in our incident runbook now.
